# Transform the Input Rather Than Cap the Search

When a search does not terminate, the reflex is to add a step limit. Sometimes the limit is
right — a genuinely exponential search needs a budget. But when non-termination comes from a
property of the *input* rather than the size of the problem, capping converts a hang into a
wrong answer, which is worse.

## The case that produced the rule

A context-free grammar recogniser searched forward from the start symbol and pruned any
sentential form whose minimum possible length exceeded the target. That is a correct pruning
and it terminates on most grammars. On `S → S S | ε` it hung: `S S S S` is longer than the
target and can still shrink back to it, so no form was ever prunable and the queue grew
forever.

A step cap would have made the recogniser return "not in the language" for strings that are
in it. The bug would have moved from a visible hang to a silent wrong answer, and the tests
would have gone green.

The fix was to change the grammar instead. Removing epsilon productions and unit productions
— both standard transformations, both preserving the language up to the empty string — leaves
a grammar in which every derivation step either lengthens the sentential form or replaces a
nonterminal by a terminal. After that the same bounded search is a genuine decision
procedure, and the bound is a consequence rather than a hope.

## How to tell which case you are in

Ask what the bound would mean if it were hit.

- **"This instance is too big for the budget I gave it"** — a cap is right, and it must
  *raise* rather than return a negative answer. Resolution saturation and SLD depth in the
  same repository do exactly that: `RuntimeError` and `DepthExceeded`, both distinct from
  "no".
- **"This input has a shape my search cannot handle"** — a cap is wrong. Normalise the input
  so the shape disappears, or the wrong answers are permanent.

## The related habit

State the boundary in the signature, not in a caveat: `max_steps`, `max_depth`,
`MAX_ENUMERABLE_VARIABLES`. And keep "out of budget" distinguishable from "no answer" — see
[[logic-for-computer-scientists]], where every bounded procedure raises rather than returning
a negative, and [[document-the-failure-mode-next-to-the-fix]] for recording why the shape
mattered once the fix has hidden the symptom.
